text:
Kaedan Korczak has 11 points in 22 games for Pittsburgh, and every one of them is an assist. That is already close to the 16 points he managed in 78 games for Vegas last season, and six of them came in his last ten.

Don't build too much on the points. His own chances are slight (1.25 expected goals), his on-ice shooting luck is close to neutral, and our range expects his scoring rate to come back toward what he has always been, with about 30 points by season's end. He has also earned some attention the other way: a Markerzone headline this month called Macklin Celebrini's "heated jabs at Kaedan Korczak" a rare sight.

The real case for him is defense. Evolving-Hockey had him 41st among 215 defensemen last season, with opponents getting 0.23 fewer expected goals per 60 when he played (97th percentile). Pittsburgh does almost five points better in expected goal share with him on the ice. The weak spot is moving the puck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him keeping possession on only 29% of exits, so watch for clears off the glass.
